introduction: To protect wildlife and forests, India has established a network of Protected Areas. The three main categories are National Parks (strictest rules), Wildlife Sanctuaries (minor human activity allowed), and Biosphere Reserves (massive areas balancing conservation with sustainable human use).

core_concepts.title: National Parks (NPs)
core_concepts.description: Areas strictly reserved for the betterment of wildlife and biodiversity. Human activities like grazing, forestry, or habitat manipulation are 'strictly prohibited'.

core_concepts.title: Wildlife Sanctuaries (WLS)
core_concepts.description: These are naturally occurring areas meant to protect specific species. Limited human activities (like collecting dry firewood or minor forest produce) are permitted as long as they don't harm the animals.

core_concepts.title: Jim Corbett - The First National Park
core_concepts.description: Established in 1936 as 'Hailey National Park' in Uttarakhand, it is India's first National Park. The Ramganga river flows through it.

core_concepts.title: The Largest and the Smallest
core_concepts.description: The largest National Park in India is 'Hemis National Park' in Ladakh (famous for Snow Leopards). The smallest is 'South Button Island National Park' in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

important_entities.name: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
important_entities.significance: Established in 1986, it spans across three states: Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. It is famous for the Lion-tailed Macaque and Nilgiri Tahr.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly tested unique fact: 'Keibul Lamjao National Park' located on Loktak Lake in Manipur is the only 'floating' national park in the world.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Madhya Pradesh (often called the Tiger State) and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands have the highest number of National Parks in India (9 or more each).

exam_strategy_tips: Jim Corbett (First NP) and Nilgiri (First Biosphere Reserve) are guaranteed questions in basic GK exams.
Remember the fundamental difference: National Parks = No human activity. Wildlife Sanctuaries = Limited human activity allowed.
